title: How David Goggins went from 297 lbs to Navy SEAL by embracing the suck and callousing his mind
summary: Goggins recounts an abusive childhood, a learning disability and a 297 lb low point. Watching Navy SEAL training pushed him to choose the hard path (the shovel) over the easy four-lane highway. He explains that growth needs friction, that you callous your mind by doing what you don't want to do daily, and that you remove every way out.

principles.text: Choose the hard path (the shovel), not the easy four-lane highway, if you want to change.
principles.quote: I chose the four-lane highway for my life the easy route the route that has gas stations throughout

principles.text: Reject managing expectations; exceed them instead.
principles.quote: not by the mindset of managing expectations by exceeding expectations not by managing them

principles.text: Train your mind to ask how you get through it, and remove every escape route.
principles.quote: I had to start training my mind to think about how the [ __ ] can I get through this not giving myself a way out

principles.text: Growth requires friction; work on weaknesses rather than only doubling down on strengths.
principles.quote: we're not going to triple down on our strengths we're not going to do that crap we're gonna work on a weaknesses so we grow we need friction to do that

principles.text: Callous your mind by doing the things you don't feel like doing, every day.
principles.quote: you don't want to study you [ __ ] study that's how you start to callus your mind

principles.text: Do something that sucks every day; embrace the suck to grow.
principles.quote: do something that sucks every single day of your life that's how you grow embrace the suck
